title: Queso Dip
subtitle: Warm melted cheese sauce with jalapeño and green pepper
excerpt: A warm, pourable melted cheese sauce with jalapeño, green pepper, cumin, and a touch of chilli powder, served with tortilla chips for dipping. Made from a simple white sauce base with cheddar melted through it.
sourceNotes: Queso dip: a melted cheese dip originating in Tex-Mex cooking, often made in the US with Velveeta (a processed cheese product) for easy melting. This version uses a standard white sauce base with mature cheddar and Gruyère for depth, which achieves the same smooth, pourable texture without processed cheese. Synthesised from standard American cooking sources adapted for UK-available ingredients.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Queso is best made just before serving. If it thickens while standing, reheat gently with a splash of milk and stir.

content.text: Queso dip is a warm, pourable cheese sauce kept smooth with a white sauce base. Without the base, cheddar melted directly in a pan splits into greasy strands. The flour and butter stabilise the sauce so it stays smooth and dippable. Grate the cheese very finely and add it off the heat; too much direct heat after the cheese goes in causes the proteins to tighten and seize.

items.prepNote: finely diced; seeds removed for mild heat

content.text: Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook the finely diced green pepper and jalapeño for 3-4 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, the cumin, and chilli powder. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the butter to the pan and let it melt. Stir in the flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. It should smell biscuity and look pale golden.

Add the milk gradually, a splash at a time, stirring after each addition until smooth. Once all the milk is in, cook on medium heat, stirring continuously, until the sauce thickens, about 4-5 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Add the grated cheddar in three additions, stirring after each until melted. Season with salt. The dip should be smooth, thick but pourable.
Serve immediately in the saucepan or a warm bowl with tortilla chips. If it thickens before serving, return to low heat and stir in a splash of milk.

items.symptom: Cheese sauce is grainy and separated
items.cause: Cheese added while the sauce was still on high heat, or added all at once
items.fix: Remove the pan from the heat completely before adding the cheese. Add in small amounts, stirring after each addition. If it's already grainy, blend with a stick blender.

items.symptom: Sauce sets solid as it cools
items.cause: Normal behaviour for a roux-based sauce
items.fix: Queso must be served immediately while warm. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of milk, stirring constantly.

items.cause: Milk added too quickly to the roux
items.fix: Add the milk slowly at first, a few tablespoons at a time, stirring until smooth before adding more. Once the first 100 ml is incorporated the rest can go in faster.

items.cause: Cheese not mature enough, or under-seasoned
items.fix: Use the most mature cheddar you have. Season with salt after the cheese is in; the cheese alone may not provide enough salt. A pinch more cumin also helps.

content.text: Queso dip is a Tex-Mex staple, served in restaurants across Texas and the American Southwest as a starter with chips. The original version uses Velveeta, a processed cheese that melts without splitting, developed by Kraft in the 1920s. Velveeta is not sold in the UK in the same form; this recipe achieves the same smooth, stable result with a standard white sauce base and mature cheddar. The flavour is considerably better.
